uncited: The method approximates the high-degree polynomial representation of the Signed Distance Field (SDF) as a quadratic equation to determine intersection existence.
It relies on affine arithmetic principles to bound the uncertainty of the polynomial coefficients over a normalized working interval.
*   Boolean `skip`: True if the ray is guaranteed not to intersect the object within the working interval.
The method operates on scalar coefficients and floating-point values.
The core data is the array of coefficients $cc_i$.
*   Calculate the discriminant $\Delta = b^2 - 4 a_{under} c$.
*   If $\Delta < 0$, there are no real roots for the underestimated polynomial.
*   If the underestimated polynomial has no roots within the working interval $[0, 1]$ (either $\Delta < 0$ or roots are outside $[0, 1]$), then the original polynomial has no roots in this interval.
*   If `skip` is False, identify the roots of the underestimated quadratic.
*   Select the smaller positive root within the working interval as `t_start`.
If $a_{under}$ is very close to zero, the quadratic formula may suffer from cancellation errors.
If the underestimated polynomial has roots, the original polynomial *might* still not have roots (false positive for intersection).
It cannot find the exact intersection point, only determine existence or provide a starting guess.
